answer: Hardware-based remote attestation mitigates Sybil creation by confining agents to secure enclaves where a cryptographic quill signs code proofs via walnut authentication. These signatures commit to an umber registry, forcing adversaries to purchase distinct physical microchips instead of spinning up free virtual machines. This binds each identity to real silicon capital costs. However, the system centralizes trust in proprietary hardware vendors and remains susceptible to side-channel leakage.
